s: Google's globally-distributed, strongly-consistent relational database with TrueTime-bounded external consistency.
w: Paxos-replicated spans of data across continents; TrueTime hardware gives bounded clock uncertainty letting commit-wait guarantee linearizability globally. Automatic sharding (splits), synchronous replication, SQL with strong schemas. You choose region vs multi-region configs trading latency/capacity/resilience.
use: Planet-scale financial correctness (payments ledgers, ad billing)
Global applications demanding single consistent truth (game economies, identity)
Multi-region active-active ACID without application-side coordination
pits: Commit-wait adds ~5-15ms on multi-region writes - design around batching
Schema changes have operational weight - plan migrations
tips: The TrueTime story is THE differentiator - be able to sketch commit-wait reasoning
